title: Library system requirements
idea: Scoping a library management system means naming who borrows, returns and reserves books, the rules for loans and fines, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Members search the catalog, borrow copies, return, renew once, and reserve titles.
The core rule: one physical copy is on at most one open loan.
A reservation queues a member for a title, served first come, first served.
Late returns earn a fine per day, capped; large unpaid fines block borrowing.

hero.title: Actors and use cases in v1

edges.caption: A member starts by finding a title and seeing how many copies are free.
If a copy is free and the member is in good standing, a loan starts.
Returning closes the loan. Days past the due date turn into a fine.

edges.label: none free
edges.caption: If every copy is out, the member joins the title's waiting queue instead.

edges.label: hand-off
edges.caption: A returned copy goes to the first waiting member, not back to the shelf.

edges.label: adds copies
edges.caption: The librarian adds copies to the catalog and handles lost or damaged items.

edges.label: expires
edges.caption: Scheduled jobs mark loans overdue and pass unclaimed pickups to the next member.
E-book lending, moving copies between branches and purchasing wait for a later version.

code.title: Use cases and policy
code.caption: The scope as code: each use case has one actor, v1 is an explicit set, and every limit is a named assumption.

walk.text: v1 is a named set. A use case missing from it is out of scope.
Print each use case with IN or OUT and the actor who starts it.
One record holds every policy number, so changing a rule means one edit.
Three actors: the member, the librarian and the system's scheduled jobs.
Nine use cases cover search, the loan cycle, reservations and fines.
Three cut features stay listed, so the cut is visible in review.
Money is a long in minor units: 1000 means 10.00 per day.

pitfalls: Do not let a reservation pin one physical copy; members wait for the title.
Write limits like 14 days or 5 loans as assumptions, not as facts.
Forgetting the system actor hides overdue marking and pickup expiry until late.

quiz.q: All copies of a title are on loan. What should v1 do when a member asks?
options: Refuse and ask the member to try again later
Add the member to a first-come queue for the title
Reserve the specific copy with the earliest due date
Shorten the current borrowers' due dates
quiz.why: A queue per title is fair and simple. Any copy that comes back serves the first waiting member, whichever copy it is.

takeaway: Agree on actors, loan rules and the one-open-loan-per-copy rule first.

starters: Should a member be able to reserve a book that has a free copy?
Which scale assumptions are sensible for a city library?
How do I explain what I left out of scope in an interview?
